A large part of hygiene is subjective, though it may not seem so at first.

In India, most people take off their shoes before entering their homes, compulsorily wash dishes with running water, use water in the washroom instead of toilet paper, and separate cooking & eating spoons.
All these are hygienic practices that many western countries don't follow, and this also give Indians the same 'perception' when they travel there.
Also, deodorant used in North America makes you smell pleasant socially, yes, but isn't really 'hygienic' as it's just masking smell instead of killing bacteria.
Powder, used in Asian countries including India is way more hygienic as it prevents moist areas for odour causing bacteria.

All this does NOT excuse our poor public sanitation & garbage collection, for sure, but how you perceive 'hygiene' is largely driven by your specific background, and it's not the same across the world
